public_rationale: The announcements support product integration at Google and Meta. They do not settle the stronger claims about strategic dependence, disregard for usefulness, and investor-driven motives across all three companies. Google's sales leader also described customer value as a priority, although that statement is neither independent verification nor evidence from the selected month.
limitations: The claim combines observable conduct with broad allegations about motives.
Company announcements establish availability more reliably than actual usefulness.
The June observation window is an interpretation, not an explicit source deadline.

statement.excerpt: Google, Microsoft and Meta have bet their futures on generative AI, cramming it into their products with little regard for utility, all to show the markets that they’re futuristic rocket ship growth companies

from_speaker: bet their futures on generative AI
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that all three companies made generative AI central to their strategies and widely integrated it, primarily to impress investors despite weak concern for usefulness.
For this ongoing, nonfinancial conduct, I use June 2024, the latest completed month before publication. Earlier announcements are context.
The metaphor about betting their futures supplies no spending threshold. Capital spending alone cannot establish disregard for usefulness or investor signaling as the principal motive.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evidence establishes substantial strategic reliance and product integration at all three companies, together with evidence that usefulness was subordinated to impressing investors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous records directly refute a material element, such as showing that a named company had not made the alleged strategic commitment. Useful individual features alone do not disprove the motive allegation.
